cover_crop: 6 monocultures (red clover, winter pea, canola, forage radish, cereal rye, oat) and 4 mixtures
comparison: cover crop treatments vs. tilled fallow (organic maize-soybean-wheat rotation)
metric: mean maize silage dry-matter yield (all treatments)
quote: Mean maize silage yield was 12.9 Mg ha-1.
note: Not an effect size itself. In pairwise comparisons only pea increased and only rye decreased maize yield vs. fallow; no mixture differed from fallow. Treatment-level yields are shown only in Fig. 1C (not extractable from text).

comparison: cover crop treatments vs. tilled fallow
metric: share of maize silage yield variability explained by cover crop treatment
quote: Cover crop treatment explained 21.7% of the variability in annual maize yield across all 3 yr (p < 0.0001; Fig. 1C).
note: Variance explained, not a yield change. Pea increased and rye decreased maize yield relative to fallow; mixtures had no effect.

comparison: cover crop biomass C/N ratio vs. maize yield
metric: maize yield variability explained by spring cover crop C/N ratio (negative correlation)
quote: Spring cover crop C/N ratio was negatively correlated with maize yield and explained 13.4% of yield variability (p < 0.0001; Fig. 1D).
note: Moderator: higher C/N (grass-dominated, ~30) cover crops lowered maize yield.

cover_crop: rye-containing vs. no-rye treatments (only cereal rye overwintered)
comparison: cover crop treatments vs. tilled fallow
metric: mean soybean yield; no cover crop effect
uncertainty: treatment effect p = 0.948; rye vs. no-rye p = 0.949
quote: Mean soybean yield was 3.1 Mg ha-1. There were no cover crop effects on soybean yield, either by treatment or between the rye-containing and no-rye treatment groups (p = 0.948 and p = 0.949, respectively), despite relatively high spring rye biomass production (2870 kg ha-1).
note: Soybean yield change vs. fallow not significant (effectively zero); C/N ratio also did not explain soybean yield (p = 0.877).

comparison: cover crop mixture vs. no cover crop
quote: A recent meta-analysis (Marcillo and Miguez, 2017) found that maize (Zea mays L.) yield increased an average of 13% following cover crop mixtures compared with no cover crop, but these were predominantly bicultures.
note: Cited from Marcillo and Miguez (2017), J. Soil Water Conserv. 72:226-239.

comparison: cover crop mixture vs. no cover crop, tilled, no fertilizer
quote: In a tilled system with no fertilizer added, Finney et al. (2016) found that cover crop mixtures with low-C/N biomass increased maize yield by up to 47%, while high-C/N mixtures decreased maize yield by up to 70%.
note: Cited from Finney et al. (2016), Agron. J. 108:39-52.

comparison: cover crop mixture vs. no cover crop, tilled, no fertilizer
quote: In a tilled system with no fertilizer added, Finney et al. (2016) found that cover crop mixtures with low-C/N biomass increased maize yield by up to 47%, while high-C/N mixtures decreased maize yield by up to 70%.
note: Cited from Finney et al. (2016). A decrease, printed as 'decreased ... by up to 70%' (i.e., -70%).
